source_document.body:

New 2027 Toyota RAV4 Cabrio Lowers Its Roof in Fantasy Land
12 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | AutoYa
The sixth-generation Toyota RAV4 will blow one candle off its birthday cake next month, as production kicked off back in December 2021.
It is currently put together not only in its local market of Japan, but also in Canada, as well as in the United States, and China. It’s based on the TNGA-K platform, just like the Camry, Highlander BEV, Crown Sport, Grand Highlander, Lexus LM, TX, TZ, NX, RX, Subaru Getaway, and other models, and as every petrolhead and their pet could tell you, it is offered in a single body style: a five-door SUV.
Could a second body style potentially join the new-gen Toyota RAV4 family? If you had asked us a few decades ago, we would have said yes. That’s because three-door versions, both with fixed-roof and convertible designs, were still a thing back then. However, given that these models are not that popular in today’s automotive world, the answer is definitely no. So, no matter how nicely you may ask the company for a different body style of the latest RAV4, they will politely decline.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | AutoYa But if such a thing is not in the making, nor even on the table, then what is up with the one pictured above in the gallery? As mentioned in the title, it lives in Fantasy Land. Thus, it is a mere rendering take on a potential open-top version of the model, which came via AutoYa on YouTube, where it was recently uploaded. The pixel artist imagined it from several angles, painted in different colors, and the cockpit is also visible in some of the digital illustrations.
Compared to the real sixth-gen Toyota RAV4, this imagined RAV4 Convertible has shorter front and rear overhangs, and a lot less space between the axles. It is also not that tall, and features an open-top view of the sky above, with a folding rag top that sits behind the rear seats when folded down. It also sports a full-size spare wheel attached to the rear door, has much thicker B-pillars, a cramped back seat with room for three occupants, and the same overall layout as the real one, albeit on a smaller scale.
It definitely has an adventurous spirit, and this thing would feel right at home in certain parts of the world. For what it’s worth, I am definitely a fan of the design, as unlike other open-top crossovers that have been launched over the years, this one is actually good to look at. Too bad Toyota does not intend to build such a thing, because a new-gen RAV4 Convertible would probably sell in sufficient numbers to justify the investment. But would you buy such a model if it were real, or would you simply ignore it?
